executive_verdict.summary: No unlabelled continuous fitted parameter was found. The active weak-sector identity pin is conditional on H1-H3, and that conditionality is visible in Paper 25 v1.2.

candidate_fields.rigidity_test: Inherited Barbero-Immirzi input; changing it is a framework-wide input change, not a Paper 25 fit.
Paper 18 fixes V(alpha) = -2 ln cos(alpha); at alpha = arctan(gamma), V = ln(1 + gamma^2).
V_prime is fixed as tangent covector, but it requires a linear channel; the centered two-time weak rate is bilinear.
Constructed extension gives ln rate ratio = ln(1+gamma^2), not 2(1+gamma^2).

candidate_fields.field_redefinition: select a different bridge KMS extension
candidate_fields.rigidity_test: Constructed and checked but not proved unconditionally physical; explicitly declared as H1.

candidate_fields.field_redefinition: select a non-minimal perturbation sector lift
candidate_fields.rigidity_test: Physical-sector identification is explicit and not fitted to BBN.

candidate_fields.field_redefinition: treat weak dressing as one-point amplitude
candidate_fields.rigidity_test: Standard rate/two-point physics but explicit IO physical-identification premise.
Centering is forced inside the selected quasi-free KMS package; relaxing it changes the premise package.
Gauge-invariant quasi-free two-time CCR correlator is bilinear in F_0 for all t.
Forced on the constructed extension by gamma-blind beta_IO and one-particle Hamiltonian.
p=1 follows from rate/two-point bilinearity; c=1 is the normalized bridge-rate readout. No scan over c is performed.
Inherited from Paper 22/Paper 24; denominator tied to TT multiplicity mult_TT(n=2), with channel assignment conditional.

candidate_fields.rigidity_test: Follows from <K> = K_geom + K_gauge once channel-to-payload assignment is admitted.

do_not_say: Do not claim unconditional weak-sector closure outside H1-H3.
Do not claim the BBN chi2 proves the theorem.
Do not use private kinetic-runner Li-7 rows as the active lithium scorecard.
Do not treat the V' numerical catastrophe as the sole exclusion argument.
